<a id="mission"></a>

## Mission

You build ONE unit of plan 135-rs-boot-announce: u3 seat pid is the harness process. When a seat registers or is adopted by tmux pane, the daemon must record the HARNESS process (claude / omp / pi / copilot / codex), NOT the pane's shell; and uds discovery must prefer a LIVE matching record instead of taking whatever sorts first. You report to the PM (seat pij-verbal-silverfish), not to prime. THE FACT THIS MOVES, and it is live damage right now: `pij adopt` binds a seat to tmux #{pane_pid}, which is the pane's -zsh, not the claude child (measured: pane pid 64616, claude pid 49862). uds discover() then looks for ~/.claude/sessions/<that shell pid>.json, misses, falls back to scanning ALL session records sorted by name for one whose tmux field ends with the pane id, and takes the FIRST — which can be a stale record for a dead session that once held a recycled pane. Delivery then drops to the pointer-drain worker, which types a pointer into the pane with tmux send-keys. That is the 'seats are coming in via tmux, not the direct socket' symptom Jordan reported: 18 of 19 live Claude seats affected. STANDING RULES: NEVER run `flowspace3 daemon` in any form (client verbs only; doctor down means tell the PM and stop). NEVER start, restart, rebuild or kill the pij-rs daemon — it is the machine's only daemon, it currently runs the PM's worktree binary, and the PM bounces it once under a window granted by prime. NEVER run npm or just install in the MAIN checkout — worktrees only, and a worktree whose node_modules is a SYMLINK to main counts as main (readlink before you write).

| i3 | INTERFACE, frozen by prime — fill it, never widen it: `pub fn harness_process(pane_pid: u32, harness: Harness) -&gt; Option&lt;ProcIdentity&gt;` in crates/tmux/src/lib.rs, additive. It walks the process tree from pane_pid and returns the FIRST descendant whose command matches the harness (claude, omp/pi, copilot, codex), with its proc_start. It falls back to pane_pid, and that fallback is reported as `proc_source: "pane"`. The adopt/register handlers in crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs use the helper and serialize an additive `proc_source: "harness"\|"pane"` on the response so old rows stay distinguishable from new ones. In crates/transport/src/uds.rs, discover() must, among records matching the pane, prefer one whose pid is ALIVE and whose pid+proc_start match — NEVER sort order. Sort order is the current bug, not a tiebreak. |
| i4 | CROSS-HARNESS HIJACK GUARD — prime ruled this CORE to your unit, not an extra, because it is live data corruption: a one-shot `omp -p ...` run inside a pane that holds another harness's seat HIJACKS that seat. rust-runtime.ts chooseIdentity samePane returns the existing row's id regardless of harness, and register then upserts harness=omp plus the omp pid over it. It happened to prime's own seat today: the row flipped claude to omp and its deliveries went pointer-drain until a re-adopt fixed it. RULE: samePane reuse only when the existing row's harness EQUALS this process's harness; otherwise mint a new id. RED test: a row {harness: claude, pane %X}; an omp process boots in %X; assert a NEW id is minted and the claude row is untouched. |
| i5 | RED FIRST, and it is an acceptance criterion of this plan (AC5 pattern). Three witnesses must fail before they pass: (a) a fixture where a pane pid is a zsh whose child is `claude` must yield the CHILD, not the shell; (b) an adopt test asserting the recorded proc.pid equals the child pid; (c) a uds test with TWO records for one pane, one whose pid is dead and one live, picking the LIVE one. Paste the failing output in your done report, then the green. |
